lessons.title: Make the next step match the effort
lessons.principle: The contact path should ask only for what the business needs in order to respond.
lessons.explanation: A repair estimate, a professional consultation, and a phone call are different amounts of effort. Choose the path the visitor can finish. A form is one option, not a requirement.
useWhen: The visitor is ready to request an estimate, appointment, or call
The business has a real response channel
avoidWhen: The page is still explaining suitability and the visitor has not been given a reason to act
requiredAssets: A real phone, email, or form endpoint from the business evidence
lessons.visitorGoal: Start the right next step without guessing which fields matter.
lessons.composition: Facts that justify the request, then one primary action. A second channel can sit quieter.
lessons.typography: The action label uses the visitor's words. Field labels are the same size as body text.
lessons.media: No image is required. Do not add a stock handshake.
lessons.mobile: The labeled action stays after the reason. Fields stack in the same order as desktop.
lessons.adaptation: If a form is too much, publish the phone or email instead. If a field is unknown, omit it.
lessons.counterexample: Placeholder-only fields, no error text, and a keyboard trap around the submit control.
lessons.counterexampleWhy: The visitor cannot tell what to enter, what failed, or how to leave.
